title: Finite-dimensional Wedderburn-Artin algebra decomposition
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $R$ be a unital $k$-algebra, not necessarily commutative, finitely generated as a $k$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Suppose that $R$ is semisimple, meaning that its regular left module is a sum of simple left ideals; simple [def-weil-pbc-simple-module] means nonzero with no nonzero proper submodule. There exist an integer $s\geq0$, integers $d_i>0$, and division $k$-algebras $D_i$ finitely generated as $k$-modules, with a $k$-algebra isomorphism $$R\simeq\prod_{i=1}^s\operatorname{Mat}_{d_i}(D_i).$$ A division $k$-algebra is a nonzero unital ring with an inverse for every nonzero element and a unital homomorphism from $k$ into its center. Matrix multiplication is the usual row-column multiplication. The empty product, a zero ring, is allowed.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Lemma 7.4.7, second reduction, p. 307: Artin-Wedderburn structure theorem; the proof cites Lam 1991, 3.5.
